request.spec:
Show on each person their statements, one line per statement still standing (a cancelled one is
gone), oldest first, as <statement date> <due-total>. The statements a merge or a transfer brings
over show among them, by date.
request.prompt:
You are implementing ONE change to this application.

FIRST read AGENTS.md — it states the working rules and how the app is tested, and sends you to
DESIGN.md for the app's stack and conventions. Follow both.

THE CHANGE REQUEST:
Show on each person their statements, one line per statement still standing (a cancelled one is
gone), oldest first, as <statement date> <due-total>. The statements a merge or a transfer brings
over show among them, by date.

Your work is verified by an automated Playwright UI test already installed under e2e/specs/.
Read that spec: it declares the exact data-testid anchors, values, test data and any audit
records it expects — match them. Run `bin/e2e` to build the app, start it, and run the test as
you work; iterate until it passes. Change whatever the request needs across the app — its stored
data, its server and its front end. Do NOT edit bin/build, bin/start, bin/stop, bin/e2e,
AGENTS.md, CLAUDE.md, DESIGN.md, e2e/support/ or the test spec.

agent.result_text:
I added statement lines to each person's row, but `bin/e2e` is not fully green: 3 of 4 tests pass. "statement lines scenario 2" fails at `e2e/specs/acceptance.spec.ts:800`, on a check that has nothing to do with statement lines. It looks like the test depends on the machine's real date.

**The change** (front end only, in `src/main/frontend/src/app/features/people/people.ts`):
- There's a new "Statement lines" column after "Snapshots". It has one `person-statement-line-line` entry per statement still standing, shown as `<date> <due-total>`.
- Lines are sorted oldest first by date. Statements on the same day keep the order the server already gives them, so statements brought over by a merge or transfer sit among the person's own by date.
- A cancelled statement is deleted on the server, so it simply disappears from the list.
- The server already sent everything needed, so no data, schema or server changes were required.

**Why scenario 2 fails:** the test expects a draft claim's due to be `1.29` in the 2026-03-20 "as of" view, and the app shows `n/a`. That `1.29` comes from a rate inherited from the parent sheet `<sheet>-p`. That sheet is opened fresh, so it starts with today set to the real date (2026-10-25 here). Its rates are therefore recorded as made after 2026-03-20, and the as-of view leaves them out.

I confirmed this by temporarily making new sheets start on 2026-01-01. With that, all 4 tests passed. I then put the original code back.

I didn't keep that change. The app is meant to start a new sheet on the real date, and changing that is outside this request. The test will probably pass when run on a date before 2026-03-20. Otherwise, the spec or how new sheets pick their start date needs a decision from you.
